chunks: Yāsīn narrated from Ḥarīz, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a slave who wanted to purchase himself, so he secretly sent a man. Does the one secretly sent have the right to buy him entirely from the slave’s wealth and not inform the master that he is only buying him from the slave’s wealth?

He عليه السلام said: “It is not proper. If he wants to render that lawful between himself and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that his wala' belongs to him, then let him add whatever he wishes, after there is an addition from his own wealth in the price of the slave. By that he makes the wala' lawful, and the wala' of the slave becomes his.”

key_terms.ثَمَنِ الْعَبْدِ: the purchase price of the slave
key_terms.فَدَسَّ إِنْسَانًا: he secretly sent a man as an intermediary
key_terms.وَلَاؤُهُ: his wala', the bond of legal allegiance connected to manumission
key_terms.يَسْتَحِلَّ: to render something lawful for oneself

ai.seo_question: Can an intermediary purchase a slave’s freedom using only the slave’s own money and still receive the wala'?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning a slave seeking freedom through an intermediary purchaser using the slave’s own money. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that this is not proper as described, and clarifies that the intermediary must contribute some of his own wealth toward the purchase price for the wala' of the freed slave to lawfully belong to him.
